requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`--config <name>` MUST select a configuration for that invocation. Otherwise,
authoring MUST use the user's selection for the canonical project root, then the
workspace default, then the user's default. Named workspace configurations MUST
override same-named user configurations as complete records. Backend, model,
connection settings, and options MUST come from the selected record as a unit;
fields MUST NOT be merged between records. Workspace-only authoring MUST work
without a user configuration file. Missing configuration or an unknown selection
MUST identify the relevant configuration file and point to documented examples.

An explicit Bedrock AWS profile or region MUST override the corresponding SDK
default; omitted values MUST use standard AWS SDK resolution. Ollama MUST use
its configured endpoint or `http://localhost:11434`. If `api_key_env` is set, its
named variable MUST supply the credential; a missing or empty value MUST produce
an error before a model request. OpenAI MUST use its configured endpoint or
`https://api.openai.com/v1`, and MUST resolve `OPENAI_API_KEY` when neither
`api_key` nor `api_key_env` is supplied.
rationale:
I found no gap against `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`. Each obligation has code reachable from the marked `{impl}` items and a test that exercises it.

**Reachability.** `main` and `author_all` reach `config::resolve_authoring` through `run_batch` and `configured_assessment`. That loads the workspace and user files and calls `resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from`. `resolve_authoring_from` delegates to the same function. Provider setup in `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider]/fn[connect]` is reached from the authoring flow. It calls `bedrock_sdk_config`, which uses `bedrock_sdk_loader`, and it calls `api_key` and `endpoint` on the Ollama and OpenAI configs.

**Selection.** All of this is in `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from]`.
- **Order:** `--config <name>` comes first, then the user's project selection for the canonical project root, then the workspace default, then the user default.
- **Workspace overrides user:** the workspace config is looked up before the user config, so a workspace record replaces a same-named user record.
- **No merging:** the whole record is taken, including `backend`, `concurrency` and `policy`.
- **Workspace only:** `user` can be `None`.
- **Errors:** for missing configuration, no selection, or an unknown name, the error names the relevant file or files and includes `CONFIG_EXAMPLES`, which points to `md/requirements/authoring.md#editing-the-file`.

**Tests for selection.**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` covers explicit, project and default selection, plus the missing-configuration error.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections]` covers workspace override and workspace-only resolution. It also covers the project > workspace default > user default order and the unknown name.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_configurations_accept_validate_and_override_concurrency]` covers whole-record replacement.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[unknown_selections_name_the_file_that_made_them]` and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[configurations_without_any_selection_report_how_to_choose_one]` cover the error messages.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` runs a workspace-only configuration through the CLI with no user file.

**Bedrock.**
- **Code:** `bedrock_sdk_loader` applies an explicit profile, region or credentials only when they are set. Otherwise it leaves the SDK's standard resolution alone.
- **Unit tests:** `providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[omitted_bedrock_profile_and_region_use_standard_sdk_resolution]` and `fn[explicit_bedrock_credentials_reach_the_sdk_without_the_default_chain]` check this against the SDK.
- **CLI tests:** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` checks the explicit profile and region on the wire. `fn[all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections]` checks the default chain.

**Ollama and OpenAI.**
- **Code:** `OllamaConfig::endpoint` falls back to `http://localhost:11434`. `OpenAiConfig::endpoint` falls back to `https://api.openai.com/v1`. `OllamaConfig::api_key_from` and `OpenAiConfig::api_key_from` read the named variable and error when it is missing or empty. OpenAI falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY` when neither `api_key` nor `api_key_env` is set. `connect` calls `api_key()?`, which runs before any completion request.
- **Tests:** `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]` checks the Ollama default endpoint. `fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` checks the OpenAI default endpoint, the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback and the missing or empty key errors. `fn[ollama_authentication_resolves_separately_and_rejects_missing_values]` checks the Ollama key variable. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_or_empty_api_key_env_fails_before_any_model_request]` shows a nonzero exit, the variable named in the error, and no connection to the model endpoint. `fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` and `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` check that `api_key_env` supplies the credential. `fn[all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections]` checks the default `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

No unspecified behavior and no `{fixme}` references turned up.
